cases.doc:
`set_recovery_escrow` was given an address that does not point back at a RecoveryEscrow
configured for this same underlying -- most likely a stale address copied from a
different market. Found during audit review: this wiring is one-shot and irreversible,
so an admin mistake here previously had no cross-check at all, unlike `initialize`.
cases.name: RecoveryEscrowMismatch

function_v0.doc:
Permissionless keeper call: extend this contract's *instance* storage (admin, config,
reserves, totals, settlement rate, fee buckets) for ~30 days. Soroban does not bump instance
TTL on ordinary reads or writes, so a long-dated market needs this called periodically (or
an archived instance restored) -- see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
function_v0.name: bump

function_v0.doc:
Forcibly move `shares` from `account`'s SY balance to the caller's own balance, without
`account`'s authorization. Callable only by the configured `RecoveryEscrow` -- this
contract does not itself verify the issuer's admin signature or check whether `account`
has actually been deauthorized; that verification happens once, in the escrow, shared
across every position type instead of duplicated here. A pure forced transfer, not a
burn: `TotalShares`/`TotalUnderlying` are unaffected, since the value stays inside the
wrapper (now credited to the escrow) until the escrow separately calls `withdraw` to
unwrap it into raw underlying.

Deliberately callable while paused: `set_paused` blocks ordinary user activity, but a
seizure already gated on caller-is-the-escrow shouldn't become unusable during an
operational pause (e.g. triggered by the same incident that justifies a legal freeze).
function_v0.name: seize

function_v0.doc:
Deposit `amount` of the underlying asset; returns shares minted to `from`. Reverts
`SlippageExceeded` if fewer than `min_shares_out` shares would be minted,
`DepositCapExceeded` if `from`'s net deposits would pass the per-address cap, and -- when
a RiskControl is wired -- `CircuitBreakerTripped`/`Paused` from RiskControl itself.
function_v0.name: deposit

function_v0.doc:
Move `amount` shares from `from` to `to`, both still subject to the same two-layer
compliance check as `deposit`/`withdraw`. This is what lets `PrincipalManager` take
custody of a user's SY shares when splitting them into PT + YT, and is otherwise a plain
SEP-41-style balance move: no change to `TotalUnderlying`/`TotalShares`, no external
token call, so there is no reentrancy surface here the way there is in deposit/withdraw.
function_v0.name: transfer

function_v0.doc:
Burn `shares` and return the equivalent underlying amount to `to`. Reverts
`SlippageExceeded` if less than `min_underlying_out` would be returned.

Releases the per-address deposit cap against `from` -- correct whenever `from` is the
real economic depositor withdrawing their own position, which is every caller of this
function today. A custodian contract unwinding SY it holds in *its own* name on behalf of
a different end user (e.g. `PrincipalManager`, between `mint` and `redeem`/`claim_yield`)
must use `withdraw_crediting` instead, or the cap release is a silent no-op against the
custodian's own (never-charged) `NetDeposited` entry -- see that function's doc comment
and `NetDeposited`'s own doc comment for the full limitation this closes. Found during
audit review.
function_v0.name: withdraw

function_v0.doc:
Initialize with the admin address, the underlying SAC address, and the Permissioning
registry used as an additional eligibility layer. `admin` must be the underlying SAC's
actual admin (`admin()`, read live) and must authorize this call -- this is what ties
market creation to the entity that actually controls the regulated asset, rather than
letting any third party stand up a market for someone else's asset.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: The per-address deposit cap in underlying units (`0` = disabled).
function_v0.name: deposit_cap

function_v0.doc:
Burn `from`'s *entire* SY balance and return the equivalent underlying to `to`. Unlike
`withdraw`, there is no `shares` argument: the authorized invocation is `(from, to,
min_underlying_out)` only, and `shares` is read live from `from`'s own balance at
execution time instead of being passed in.

This exists for callers -- in practice, Router functions that chain a `MarketPool` swap's
output straight into a withdrawal -- where the swap's payout is a curve-derived amount:
`MarketPool`'s price depends on `seconds_to_maturity`, read live from the ledger, so the
exact payout computed during a client's pre-submission simulation can differ by a few raw
units from what real execution computes moments later. Passing that payout as an explicit
`shares` argument to `withdraw` would need Soroban's pre-signed authorization for *that*

function_v0.doc: Current exchange rate: underlying units per share, scaled by RATE_SCALE.

function_v0.doc:
Underlying `account` has deposited, net of what it withdrew (floored at 0). This is the
quantity the per-address cap applies to.

Released correctly by `withdraw`/`withdraw_all`/`withdraw_gained` whenever `account` is
the address that actually calls one of those functions (the ordinary case). It is
*not* released by a plain `withdraw`-family call made by some other custodian contract on
`account`'s behalf while holding `account`'s SY in the custodian's own name -- e.g.

release against the manager's own `NetDeposited` entry -- which was never charged -- so

function_v0.doc: Set the per-address deposit cap (underlying units); `0` disables it. Existing balances\nabove a newly lowered cap are not clawed back -- the cap only gates further deposits.
function_v0.name: set_deposit_cap

function_v0.doc:
Withdraw only the SY `from` gained *since* `baseline` -- the balance `from` already held
before whatever produced the gain, read by the caller (typically a Router composing a
wrap-then-flash-mint flow) via a plain `balance_of` call immediately before that step.

Unlike `withdraw_all`, pre-existing SY above `baseline` is left untouched, so a caller
who already holds unrelated SY for another position does not need to clear it first --
found to matter live while composing `Router.flash_mint_yt_from_underlying`: its surplus
(the wrapped budget minus the real net cost) could previously only be swept with
`withdraw_all`, which refuses to run at all if the caller holds any other SY, costing an
extra signature to clear it first.

`shares = balance_of(from) - baseline` is computed internally rather than taken as a

function_v0.name: withdraw_gained

function_v0.doc:
Wire the RiskControl this wrapper reports deposits to. The wrapper must also be registered
as a consumer on that RiskControl (`RiskControl.add_consumer`) or every deposit reverts.

Unlike `set_recovery_escrow`, this is updatable (no "already set" guard), so a wrong
address here is not irreversible the same way -- but an admin mistake (e.g. a copy-pasted
address of some other contract entirely) would otherwise only surface the next time a
user deposits. This calls back into the given address's own `is_consumer` -- the one
read-only view every real RiskControl exposes -- so a non-RiskControl address (wrong
contract type, unrelated address) fails this call instead of silently being wired in.
Deliberately does not require the *result* to be `true`: every deployment path in this
repo (see `scripts/create_market.sh`, `MarketFactory`) calls `set_risk_control` before the
matching `RiskControl.add_consumer`, so this wrapper is not registered yet at this point.
function_v0.name: set_risk_control

function_v0.doc:
Same as `withdraw`, except the per-address deposit-cap release is credited to
`beneficiary` instead of `from`. For a custodian contract that holds SY in its own name on
behalf of a specific end user -- today, only `PrincipalManager`'s `redeem` (the PT leg) and
its internal `pay_yield` (the YT leg and `claim_yield`) -- `from` here is the custodian's
own address, not the real depositor who originally paid into the per-address cap at
`deposit` time. Crediting `from` (plain `withdraw`'s behavior) would be a no-op against an
address whose `NetDeposited` was never charged, leaving the real depositor's cap stuck at
its deposited level forever, even after they fully exit -- found during audit review (see
`NetDeposited`'s doc comment). `beneficiary` does not need any standing of its own here:
it is only a storage key for the release, not a party to the transfer.

rather than an extra parameter threaded through the one common functio
function_v0.name: withdraw_crediting

function_v0.doc:
One-time wiring of the RecoveryEscrow contract authorized to call `seize`. Mirrors the
`set_minter` pattern used on PTToken/YTToken: settable once, never reassigned, breaking
the circular dependency between SYWrapper and RecoveryEscrow at deployment time -- which
also means an admin mistake here (wrong address, a stale address copied from a different
market) is otherwise permanent. Mirroring `PrincipalManager::initialize`'s
`assert_topology_matches` and `RecoveryEscrow::initialize`'s own cross-check of every
position's `underlying_address()`, this calls back into the given address and requires its
own `underlying_address()` to match this wrapper's underlying before accepting it. Found
during audit review.
function_v0.name: set_recovery_escrow
